title: Shutdown and Trade Risk
brief: Which players could be shut down late in the season or traded before the deadline, and how does that affect their value for our March 28 end? It must flag who matters most for playoff weeks 19 to 21 and which young players could gain if a veteran is moved.
summary: Our season ends 2027-03-28, so late-season rest falls inside our playoffs (weeks 19 to 21), and every move made before the 2027-03-04 trade deadline happens before them. Pay no more than the stated ranges for veterans on teams with nothing to play for in March, mainly Brooklyn, Milwaukee and Golden State. Plan to trade those players before March 4, and save FAB for the players who gain minutes when a veteran is moved.

sections.heading: Why March risk hits us harder

paragraphs.text: Our fantasy playoffs are weeks 19, 20 and 21, and they end on 2027-03-28. The trade deadline is 2027-03-04, so any deadline trade changes a player's role before our playoffs start. Late-season rest falls in our playoff weeks themselves. Projections have to assume that trade candidates stay all season, so they miss this risk. For stars on bad teams, the experts want value ranges that include the chance of rest and cut minutes, not just per-game value.

Two kinds of team cause the risk. First, once a team decides to tank, it may shut down injured players for the rest of the season, even if they could have come back. Second, some teams do not control their own pick: the Nets, Bucks, Clippers, Pelicans and Mavericks. They have no reason to tank and no reason to push for wins. They may rest players, be extra careful with injuries, or give young players more minutes late in the season. The notes name Brooklyn and Milwaukee as the main examples.

Here is the rule for our league. A team with no reason to win or lose in March can cut veteran minutes to develop young players, so value its veterans lower. Suppose a veteran on a tanking team, or on a team without its own pick, gets hurt in February or March. Assume he may not return before March 28. Do not hold him in a starting slot while you wait.

sections.heading: Shutdown risk in playoff weeks 19 to 21

paragraphs.text: Brooklyn carries the clearest March risk. Julius Randle may sit some March games so young players get time, and Brooklyn plays only 10 games across our three playoff weeks. Michael Porter Jr. shares that light schedule. Keep both inside their 10 to 15 USD ranges. If you are contending, plan to trade one of them before 2027-03-04.

Golden State may rest its veterans. Stephen Curry played 43 games last season, and the team has 15 back-to-backs. His playoff schedule is good, though. Bid 25 to 31 USD and do not chase last year's 42 USD. Draymond Green is a 1 USD final pick at most, because the Warriors may rest veterans in a gap year. Al Horford's rest on back-to-backs caps him at about 60 games, so leave him on waivers.

The Clippers and Mavericks do not own their picks. For Darius Garland the experts call the late-rest risk small, so high teens is still fine and 25 USD is the ceiling. Kyrie Irving's Dallas has 16 back-to-backs, the most in the league, plus a 4-4-4 playoff schedule. In the first weeks, track how often he sits and how many minutes he plays. That decides how much of the 4-4-4 he actually plays.

sections.heading: Trade candidates in the auction pool

paragraphs.text: Several early-round players carry trade tags. Moore thinks Denver could move Jamal Murray to shed salary. Austin Reaves is a trade risk if the Lakers are not working. The Pelicans reportedly ask about three firsts and a young player for Trey Murphy III. The notes do not cut their prices for this risk, so the ranges stand: Murray at 34 to 38 USD, Reaves up to 36 USD with 40 USD as an overpay, and Murphy in the low 20s USD. Check trade news for all three before the deadline.

For some players, a trade would shrink the role. A move to a contender would cut Norman Powell's value right before our playoffs, so stay at 3 to 7 USD. A trade could cut Michael Porter Jr.'s usage further. A trade could shrink Cameron Johnson's role, so he is a 1 to 2 USD last pick. If Dallas trades Daniel Gafford, drop him for waiver centers.

Milwaukee does not own its pick and needs to consolidate its roster. The trade tags cover Ryan Rollins, whose cheap contract could bring first-round picks, and Tyler Herro, who could be moved at the deadline. They also cover Kevin Porter Jr., Jaime Jaquez Jr. (possibly to Denver), Kyle Kuzma, Kasparas Jakučionis and AJ Green. Bid on Rollins in the low to mid teens and on Herro at 10 to 15 USD. Treat Kevin Porter Jr. as a 1 to 3 USD flyer and Jaquez as a 1 USD flyer. Re-check this group every week from February to March 4.

Some cheaper trade candidates are still worth buying. Rudy Gobert could be traded if Minnesota's season goes badly. Bid 8 to 12 USD, and plan around his two-game semifinal week (week 20). Ty Jerome does not fit Memphis's young core at 29, but Memphis plays 4-4-4 in our playoffs, so a bid up to 11 USD is fine. Orlando sits near the second apron and may choose Anthony Black over Jalen Suggs. Pay 5 to 9 USD for Suggs and plan for about 20 missed games.

Anthony Davis: the experts expect him to stay in Washington, but the Wizards could reconsider near the deadline. Either way, a fair price is 26 to 30 USD. Do not pay near ESPN's value or last year's 54 USD. Early on, check how often the Q (Rest) status costs him games.

Domantas Sabonis: one side points to Toronto talks and the risk that a contender uses him as a backup. Lloyd thinks his contract makes a trade unlikely. Low 30s USD is fine and 40 USD is not, because a backup role before our playoffs would hurt.

Zach LaVine: the experts disagree on whether the rebuilding Kings will pull his minutes or sit veterans. A trade, buyout or benching is also possible. At 5 to 12 USD the risk is priced in. Watch for trade or buyout news, and check that he stays near 30 or more minutes.

sections.heading: Who gains when a veteran moves

paragraphs.text: Projections assume trade candidates stay all season, so they can understate the young players behind them. Teams without their own pick may also shift late-season minutes to young players. The notes name who is next in line: Burries behind Herro, Caleb Wilson for usage next to Powell, Anthony Black next to Suggs, Leonard Miller next to Jalen Smith, Wells next to Jerami Grant, Ware next to Kuzma and Daniels next to Dort. None of them is in our draft table. Treat them as FAB targets, not auction targets.

Some undrafted players on our list become adds only if a trade or injury opens a role. AJ Green is worth a pickup only if he gets starter minutes. Miles McBride is worth one if a trade opens a starting role, though the Knicks' playoff schedule is weak. Zach Collins needs a trade to a team with real center minutes. Kasparas Jakučionis needs a move to a clearer role. Mark Williams is out until mid to late March, but if he returns healthy, Phoenix plays 4-4-4 in weeks 19 to 21. Expect him to be a backup, though.

Concrete plan. Keep part of your FAB budget for the days after 2027-03-04, because waivers run daily. You get at most 6 adds per week, so spend them on the players whose roles grow. Before the deadline, use the active trade market to sell veterans on teams with nothing to play for, such as Brooklyn and Milwaukee, if you expect to make the playoffs.
